chapters.title: Chapter 562: Labyrinth of Avarice
paragraphs: The portal dropped Leon into the next trial without warning.
He went from standing inside the restless glow of the third-floor gate to solid stone beneath his boots. Behind him, the light folded in on itself and disappeared with a quiet sigh.

A round chamber surrounded him, about thirty paces from one side to the other. Cleanly carved stone blocks made up the walls and continued overhead into a shallow dome. Nothing showed the passage of time. There was no dust in the seams, no cracks, and no worn edges. Whatever maintained the Ascension Tower kept this place untouched.
Three doors had been placed evenly around the room.
Dark bronze formed the first, and a key had been engraved across its center.
The second door was silver. Its symbol showed an open treasure chest.
The last one was black from edge to edge.

No light came back from its surface. Leon couldn’t find a handle, hinges, or even a clear border where the door met the frame. His eyes kept slipping away whenever he looked at it. He had to make a conscious effort to hold his gaze there.
Before he moved closer, text appeared in front of him.
[ASCENSION TOWER — FLOOR THREE]
[Trial: Labyrinth of Avarice]
[Collect three Tower Keys.]
[Reach the central gate.]
[Defeat the Gatekeeper to clear Floor Three.]
[Optional treasures may be claimed throughout the labyrinth.]
[Every optional treasure claimed will strengthen the Gatekeeper.]
[Death within the trial is permanent.]
[Adaptive Calibration Active.]
[Trials and guardians will adjust to the challenger’s demonstrated capabilities.]
Leon went over the message twice.
The conditions themselves weren’t complicated. Find three keys, reach the center, and kill the Gatekeeper. Everything else was optional.

The calibration notice mattered more. Floor Three would not send ordinary Ascendant- or Sage-rank obstacles against him and pretend they were meaningful. Its constructs, traps, and trial pressure would scale to what he demonstrated. Rank alone would be a poor measure inside the labyrinth.

Anyone focused only on survival would take the bronze paths, gather the necessary keys, and leave the extra rewards alone. That route would keep the final enemy as weak as possible and offer the safest way upward.
The silver door represented the other choice.

Treasures would improve Leon’s strength, but each one would also improve the Gatekeeper. The Tower wasn’t hiding what it wanted. It placed greed in front of every challenger, then charged them for giving in.
At least it tells me how it plans to punish me.
He didn’t choose immediately. First, Leon spread his spatial awareness across the chamber.

The entire room settled into his perception. He traced the exact curve of the dome, measured the chamber’s dimensions, and caught the tiny joins between each fitted block. With a thought, he folded the distance to the opposite wall, brought it briefly closer, then let space return to normal.
His control felt as steady as ever.
He directed that awareness toward the bronze door.
It reached the threshold and stopped.

The silver door blocked him in the same way. When he tested the black one, the result was worse. His perception touched the flat surface and simply disappeared. Nothing from beyond the door reached him.

Leon returned his attention to the bronze entrance. He couldn’t sense through it, but its placement gave him a rough idea of where the passage on the other side should start. He tried forming a fold across that short gap.
The connection ran into something absolute.
There was no resistance he could push through. He found no formation to study, no barrier to dismantle. At the doorway, his authority over space ceased to matter.
He maintained the unfinished fold for several seconds, then released it.
The Tower’s authority takes priority over mine.
Fair enough. Keys and locked routes wouldn’t mean much if a spatial user could skip the entire labyrinth and appear beside the central gate.
His abilities should still work inside any section he had already entered. They just wouldn’t carry him through boundaries the Tower had sealed.
With that settled, Leon crossed the chamber to the black door.

Up close, its empty surface looked even less natural. He pressed his palm against it. The material was perfectly smooth, but it gave him nothing else. No heat. No chill. Not even the faintest vibration.
Mana failed to stir it.
Holy energy sank into the black surface and vanished.

Through Void Dominion, Leon pressed against the space around the doorway. Every fold ended at the same invisible limit. Even the authority he possessed as a challenger inside the Tower produced nothing.
The door wasn’t fighting him.
It simply didn’t recognize him as someone capable of using it.
Leon lowered his hand and took a step back.

The bronze door displayed a key. The silver one displayed treasure. Both made their purpose obvious. The black door explained nothing at all. In a place built with as much intent as the Ascension Tower, that couldn’t be meaningless.
There was something behind it.
He committed the door’s measurements to memory, along with the strange sensation of its surface. For now, he lacked whatever was needed to open it. Standing there longer wouldn’t solve that problem.
Only two real choices remained.
Leon looked once at the key engraved on the bronze door, then faced the silver door and its open chest.
The warning had been clear. Taking an optional reward would make the Gatekeeper stronger. There was nothing dishonest about the exchange.

And a treasure from the Ascension Tower probably wasn’t some common trinket. Leon hadn’t come here to take the safest route available and avoid every meaningful risk. He wanted rewards that justified entering the Tower in the first place.
More importantly, walking away without even checking what waited beyond the silver door would annoy him far more than fighting an empowered enemy later.
"It’d be impolite not to take a look," Leon said.
His palm touched the silver door.
It opened without making a sound.

A narrow stone passage stretched beyond it. The floor was made from shifting tiles, with full rows sliding side to side in patterns that kept changing. Fine wires ran between the walls at several heights. In the weak light, some were almost impossible to see. A few floor stones rested slightly below the others, revealing pressure mechanisms beneath them.
Space itself had also been trapped.

Small distortions hung throughout the corridor, bending direction and distance around their edges. Anyone who stepped into one carelessly might be turned sideways, hurled into a wire, or deposited directly onto a pressure plate.
Leon stayed at the doorway and sent his awareness into the corridor.

It wasn’t a collection of separate traps. The whole passage worked as one moving system. Each sliding row altered the safe path, while several pressure plates waited exactly where someone in a rush would naturally place a foot.
At the far end, the corridor opened into another room.
A pale blue object floated above a pedestal there.
The Tower had placed the reward where it could be seen from the entrance.
A faint smile touched Leon’s mouth. It wanted challengers staring at the prize while they hurried through the danger.
He watched one complete cycle of the moving floor before stepping inside.
The first stretch gave him little trouble. He cleared two pressure plates, bent beneath a wire, and paused until a sliding row lined up with the next safe section.
The timing changed before the cycle should have ended.
Stone started dropping under his right foot.

Leon folded the gap between his position and the next safe tile. He slid across the shortened distance as spikes burst from both walls. One blade scraped his bronze-gold sleeve before he escaped their path. It left a thin line that his conscious armor erased almost at once.
A moment later, the spikes disappeared back into the walls.
Leon glanced at the narrow tear along his arm.
Nothing had malfunctioned. The corridor had let him trust the pattern, waited for him to commit, and then changed the timing.
"So you adjust too."
The labyrinth offered no reply.

He continued, but no longer treated the patterns as fixed rules. His experience guided his pace and kept him from trying to force a quick crossing. Leon watched each tile until the final instant, ready to change direction whenever the corridor reacted to what he expected.
Halfway through, three wires had been arranged to block every reasonable route.

Rather than touch them, Leon folded the space around the highest one. Its anchors stayed where they were, but he bent the distance between them enough to shift the wire’s path by several inches. That gave him just enough room to pass. Once he was clear, he released the fold and let the corridor return to its original shape.
The pale blue treasure became easier to make out with every step.
So did the thing waiting behind it.

A long metal creature stood near the chamber’s rear wall. It had the shape of a thin hound, though each front leg ended in a narrow blade instead of a paw. Leon saw no eyes, no mouth, and no heat coming from its body.
He halted on the corridor’s final tile.
The creature disappeared.
Without crossing the intervening distance, it appeared again three paces to one side.
A notification formed before Leeon.
[Optional Guardian: Blinksteel Stalker]
Its smooth, featureless head turned in his direction.
Leon drew his sword.

The force concentrated inside the construct sat comfortably in Ethereal Initiate territory, far above anything appropriate for an ordinary third-floor challenger. Leon had handled enemies at that rank with ease before several of his later upgrades. Raw power alone did not concern him.
The way the creature moved did.
The creature vanished once more.

He directed that awareness toward the bronze door.
It reached the threshold and stopped.
The silver door blocked him in the same way.
When he tested the black one, the result was worse.
His perception touched the flat surface and simply disappeared.
Nothing from beyond the door reached him.
Leon returned his attention to the bronze entrance.
He couldn’t sense through it, but its placement gave him a rough idea of where the passage on the other side should start.
He tried forming a fold across that short gap.
The connection ran into something absolute.
There was no resistance he could push through.
He found no formation to study, no barrier to dismantle.
At the doorway, his authority over space ceased to matter.
He maintained the unfinished fold for several seconds, then released it.
The Tower’s authority takes priority over mine.
Fair enough.
Keys and locked routes wouldn’t mean much if a spatial user could skip the entire labyrinth and appear beside the central gate.
His abilities should still work inside any section he had already entered.
They just wouldn’t carry him through boundaries the Tower had sealed.
With that settled, Leon crossed the chamber to the black door.
Up close, its empty surface looked even less natural.
He pressed his palm against it.
The material was perfectly smooth, but it gave him nothing else.
No heat.
No chill.
Not even the faintest vibration.
Mana failed to stir it.
Holy energy sank into the black surface and vanished.
Through Void Dominion, Leon pressed against the space around the doorway.
Every fold ended at the same invisible limit.
Even the authority he possessed as a challenger inside the Tower produced nothing.
The door wasn’t fighting him.
It simply didn’t recognize him as someone capable of using it.
Leon lowered his hand and took a step back.
The bronze door displayed a key.
The silver one displayed treasure.
Both made their purpose obvious.
The black door explained nothing at all.
In a place built with as much intent as the Ascension Tower, that couldn’t be meaningless.
There was something behind it.
He committed the door’s measurements to memory, along with the strange sensation of its surface.
For now, he lacked whatever was needed to open it.
Standing there longer wouldn’t solve that problem.
Only two real choices remained.
Leon looked once at the key engraved on the bronze door, then faced the silver door and its open chest.
The warning had been clear.
Taking an optional reward would make the Gatekeeper stronger.
There was nothing dishonest about the exchange.
And a treasure from the Ascension Tower probably wasn’t some common trinket.
Leon hadn’t come here to take the safest route available and avoid every meaningful risk.
He wanted rewards that justified entering the Tower in the first place.
More importantly, walking away without even checking what waited beyond the silver door would annoy him far more than fighting an empowered enemy later.
"It’d be impolite not to take a look," Leon said.
His palm touched the silver door.
It opened without making a sound.
A narrow stone passage stretched beyond it.
The floor was made from shifting tiles, with full rows sliding side to side in patterns that kept changing.
Fine wires ran between the walls at several heights.
In the weak light, some were almost impossible to see.
A few floor stones rested slightly below the others, revealing pressure mechanisms beneath them.
Space itself had also been trapped.
Small distortions hung throughout the corridor, bending direction and distance around their edges.
Anyone who stepped into one carelessly might be turned sideways, hurled into a wire, or deposited directly onto a pressure plate.
Leon stayed at the doorway and sent his awareness into the corridor.
It wasn’t a collection of separate traps.
The whole passage worked as one moving system.
Each sliding row altered the safe path, while several pressure plates waited exactly where someone in a rush would naturally place a foot.
At the far end, the corridor opened into another room.
A pale blue object floated above a pedestal there.
The Tower had placed the reward where it could be seen from the entrance.
A faint smile touched Leon’s mouth.
It wanted challengers staring at the prize while they hurried through the danger.
He watched one complete cycle of the moving floor before stepping inside.
The first stretch gave him little trouble.
He cleared two pressure plates, bent beneath a wire, and paused until a sliding row lined up with the next safe section.
The timing changed before the cycle should have ended.
Stone started dropping under his right foot.
Leon folded the gap between his position and the next safe tile.
He slid across the shortened distance as spikes burst from both walls.
One blade scraped his bronze-gold sleeve before he escaped their path.
It left a thin line that his conscious armor erased almost at once.
A moment later, the spikes disappeared back into the walls.
Leon glanced at the narrow tear along his arm.
Nothing had malfunctioned.
The corridor had let him trust the pattern, waited for him to commit, and then changed the timing.
"So you adjust too."
The labyrinth offered no reply.
He continued, but no longer treated the patterns as fixed rules.
His experience guided his pace and kept him from trying to force a quick crossing.
Leon watched each tile until the final instant, ready to change direction whenever the corridor reacted to what he expected.
Halfway through, three wires had been arranged to block every reasonable route.
Rather than touch them, Leon folded the space around the highest one.
Its anchors stayed where they were, but he bent the distance between them enough to shift the wire’s path by several inches.
That gave him just enough room to pass.
Once he was clear, he released the fold and let the corridor return to its original shape.
The pale blue treasure became easier to make out with every step.
So did the thing waiting behind it.
A long metal creature stood near the chamber’s rear wall.
It had the shape of a thin hound, though each front leg ended in a narrow blade instead of a paw.
Leon saw no eyes, no mouth, and no heat coming from its body.
He halted on the corridor’s final tile.
The creature disappeared.
Without crossing the intervening distance, it appeared again three paces to one side.
A notification formed before Leeon.
[Optional Guardian: Blinksteel Stalker]
Its smooth, featureless head turned in his direction.
Leon drew his sword.
The force concentrated inside the construct sat comfortably in Ethereal Initiate territory, far above anything appropriate for an ordinary third-floor challenger.
Leon had handled enemies at that rank with ease before several of his later upgrades.
Raw power alone did not concern him.
The way the creature moved did.
The creature vanished once more.

chapters.title: Chapter 563: Blinksteel Stalker
paragraphs: Leon was already moving when the Stalker returned.
He shortened the space to his left and slipped away from the corridor’s final tile. A silver foreblade passed through the spot his ribs had occupied barely a moment before.
Instead of flesh, it struck one of the wires.
The impact sent a clear metallic note through the passage.
Every trap still waiting in the corridor triggered together.

Floor tiles dropped. Blades shot from the walls. The warped areas of space widened until they crowded the route behind him. Leon twisted through the sudden chaos, but the Stalker had disappeared once more.
His integrated combat experience warned him before his senses found anything.
Leon turned and brought up his sword.
The construct appeared at his back, both bladed forelimbs sweeping for his neck. His sword caught the first. The second kept coming toward his shoulder.
Space stretched around Leon’s body.
Only a little distance remained between him and the blade, but he lengthened it enough. The edge swept across the front of his chest instead of cutting through him.
Leon drove a kick into the creature’s narrow torso. The blow knocked it out of the corridor and sent it skidding across the chamber floor.
He went after it immediately, unwilling to let the passage spring something else on him.

He could have opened with Leximancy or buried the construct beneath far more elemental force. Instead, he kept those options in reserve. A spatial guardian stood between him and a spatial treasure, and its current attacks were not getting through his armor. As long as that remained true, learning how its movement worked was worth more than ending the exchange one breath earlier.
As soon as both boots entered the room, everything behind him went still. The shifting rows locked into place. Wall blades pulled back, and the spatial distortions collapsed until none remained.
Near the pedestal, the Stalker pushed itself upright.

With the corridor no longer demanding his attention, Leon spread his spatial awareness through the construct. Energy traveled along fine channels inside its silver-gray frame, passing between the torso and limbs. Almost all of them gathered under its wedge-shaped head, where several metal layers protected a dense knot.
That had to be the core.
Before Leon could study it any longer, the Stalker disappeared.
It didn’t accelerate or leave behind a blur. It was simply across the room, then beside him. One of its blades was already cutting for his ribs when it arrived.
Leon met it with his sword.

The collision carried the force of an Ethereal Initiate and sent a hard vibration through his armor. The guardian’s thin body hid far more weight than it appeared to carry. It had also attacked from an angle that no creature approaching on foot could have managed.
Leon started a counterstrike.
The Stalker vanished before his blade reached it, leaving him to cut through empty air.
It appeared behind him again.
Nine integrated years of battle turned recognition into movement before conscious thought caught up. His stance dropped, his hips turned, and his sword rose into the descending forelimb.
Metal slammed against metal.
Leon stepped back and guided the force past his body. The Stalker touched down, visible for no more than an instant, then jumped away again.
His awareness could follow anything that crossed ordinary distance.
The Stalker crossed none.
For a fraction of a heartbeat during every jump, it disappeared entirely from Leon’s perception. Once he found it again, the next strike had already begun.
A blade came in from the right.
Leon curved the space along its path.
The weapon’s arc shifted several inches away from him. Instead of reaching his side, the blade continued into the guardian’s own flank.
A shrill scrape tore through the chamber as metal cut against metal.
The Stalker stumbled aside. A deep groove now ran along its body.
Leon moved in to exploit the opening.
The construct vanished before his sword could reach the damaged section.
It returned at a greater distance this time. One foreblade sat at a changed angle, while the other had been drawn tight against its torso.
Their next clash proved what Leon had begun to suspect.

He bent the path of another strike, but the Stalker altered its motion halfway through. The fold still dragged the blade aside, just not enough. Its edge scraped across his conscious armor and left a bright streak over the bronze-gold surface. The mark vanished as the armor repaired itself.
The guardian was adapting.

Leon blocked the next attack, then gave ground without trying to answer it. Pursuing the Stalker through every exchange was pointless. Whenever the situation turned against it, the construct could jump somewhere safer.
Predicting the attacks wasn’t enough.
He needed to know where the creature would appear.
Leon pushed his spatial awareness to cover the whole chamber.

Any spatial fold disturbed the area around it. Leon crossed distance by compressing the gap between two places, then letting it settle behind him. The Stalker’s method wasn’t the same, but its jumps left a related sign. A tiny seam opened at the destination to receive its body.
That opening lasted almost no time at all.
But it formed before the Stalker arrived.
The construct jumped.
Leon let its disappearance go and searched the room instead.
A seam opened beside his left shoulder.
He turned quickly enough to stop the first blade. The second slammed into his side and drove him backward. His armor took most of the force, though pain still spread along his ribs.
The discomfort faded almost immediately. Nothing in the strike had pierced the conscious plate or exceeded what his body could repair.
The approach worked.
His body just needed to keep up with it.
Attack after attack followed. The Stalker emerged from a new angle every time. Leon no longer tried to damage it. He blocked, moved back, and watched how the chamber changed before each arrival.
His integrated combat experience covered details conscious thought could not process fast enough.

Nine years of remembered battle let him pick meaning out of the guardian’s stance before it vanished. When its front half dipped slightly, the next attack would begin from above. A twist in its thin torso came before an appearance at Leon’s back. Even the position of its foreblades indicated whether the jump would be short or long.
Those signs gave him the small amount of time he had been missing.
The Stalker lowered itself, both blades turned inward.
Then it disappeared.
A destination seam began opening directly ahead of Leon.
He had already prepared for it.

Leon compressed the space around the forming point. He didn’t close it off. If he blocked the jump completely, the Stalker could simply abandon that destination and choose another. Instead, he allowed just enough room for the transfer to complete while tightening everything around it.
The construct appeared inside the compressed space.
Pressure closed in from every side. Its jump succeeded, but its legs couldn’t spread far enough to support a proper landing. The raised blades also lost most of their reach.
Leon’s sword had begun its strike before the Stalker fully emerged.
A thin white line of holy energy gathered along the edge.
He stepped inside the guardian’s shortened range and drove the point upward beneath its wedge-shaped head. His target was the knot where all the internal channels met.
The sword struck the outer shell.
The metal held.
Leon kept pressing and sent a controlled pulse of holy energy through the point. The casing around the core split, and the sword broke through.
The Blinksteel Stalker convulsed.
One foreblade lashed at him without aim. Compressed space slowed the attack enough for Leon to lean away. He twisted the sword inside the guardian and released another pulse.
The core broke apart.
Energy flashed down every channel in the Stalker’s frame. Its limbs locked in place, and whatever had powered the blades vanished.
Leon let the spatial compression go.
The construct hit the stone floor.
He kept his sword ready and watched it.
Nothing moved.

Leon finally breathed out and rolled his shoulder out of habit. The guardian hadn’t demanded his full power. It had demanded attention and control. That was likely intentional. Someone who crushed it immediately would gain less from the fight than someone who learned what its movement actually did.
The pale blue crystal above the pedestal stopped rotating.
Notifications appeared in front of him.
[Optional Guardian Defeated: Blinksteel Stalker]
[Optional Treasure Available]
[Spatial Tempering Crystal — Epic]
[Effect: Strengthens spatial comprehension and permanently increases resistance to hostile spatial manipulation when absorbed.]
Behind Leon, the Stalker’s remains slowly lost their heat while he examined the crystal.
An Epic treasure, already available on the third floor.
The Ascension Tower had shown him the reward.
Now he had to decide whether claiming it was worth making the Gatekeeper stronger.

chapters.title: Chapter 564: Leaving Money on the Table
paragraphs: Leon crossed the chamber and came to a stop at the pedestal.

The Spatial Tempering Crystal turned slowly above its surface. Pale-blue light drifted through the crystal, tracing darker veins within it. Those lines seemed to curve whenever Leon shifted his angle.
He didn’t need to touch the treasure to notice its effect. The space around it was already reacting to him.
The Tower had picked its bait well.

An ordinary reward would have been easier to leave behind after that warning. This crystal offered something tied directly to one of Leon’s strongest abilities. It could improve his understanding of space and permanently increase his resistance to hostile spatial manipulation.
The cost would appear later, at the central gate.
Leon looked back at the ruined Stalker.

The guardian had been dangerous in the way an adaptive Tower construct could be, but it had never brought him close to dying. Most of its threat came from the way its jumps disrupted his spatial awareness. Once he figured out what the creature was doing, the fight became much easier to control.
If the Gatekeeper gained something similar, Leon would at least understand the mechanic already.
He reached for the crystal and closed his hand around it.
[Optional Treasure Acquired]
[Spatial Tempering Crystal — Epic]
It fit easily in his palm. The cool surface hummed faintly against his fingers, and Void Dominion stirred in response as if it had recognized something familiar.
Leon didn’t absorb it.

An Epic treasure could cause a major change. Trying to understand and integrate one in the middle of an unexplored trial would be needlessly reckless. He stored the crystal as it was and decided to examine it somewhere safer.
The Tower answered immediately.
[Optional Treasures Claimed: 1]
[Gatekeeper Enhancement Applied]
[The Gatekeeper has acquired Spatial Resistance.]
Leon’s expression tightened.
The warning had only said that each treasure would strengthen the Gatekeeper. It hadn’t said the enhancement would be directly connected to the reward.
This wasn’t a simple increase in strength.

Because the Stalker had guarded a spatial treasure, claiming it granted the Gatekeeper Spatial Resistance. The other optional chambers would probably work the same way. Each treasure Leon collected could add another related defense or ability to the final enemy.
Take enough rewards, and the Gatekeeper might become a mixture of every optional challenge on the floor.
That made the choice more dangerous than Leon had first thought.
It also made the final fight sound much more interesting.

Interesting did not mean he would claim everything blindly. One reward had given him something directly useful. From this point on, every optional route would have to justify both its own danger and the ability it granted the Gatekeeper.

He left the pedestal and returned to the Stalker’s body. Before moving on, he wanted another look at the guardian’s core. Its internal structure might prove useful once he eventually absorbed the crystal.
The metal beneath its head had split where Leon’s sword went through. Broken channels spread around the destroyed core, most of them dark now that the construct’s energy had disappeared.
Something black rested among them.
Leon crouched beside the remains.

The object hadn’t been inside the core. It had been hidden behind it. His earlier spatial examination missed the thing because it carried no energy and blended into the empty space around the Stalker’s central mechanisms.
He eased it loose.

It was a narrow shard of black material, a little longer than his thumb. One side was perfectly smooth. The opposite edge had broken unevenly. A faint design had been pressed into its surface, but the marking ended at the fracture before it could form anything he recognized.
No mana came from it.
There was no aura or spiritual presence either.
Even its weight felt hard to measure.
Leon rubbed a thumb over the flawless surface.
The sealed black door came to mind at once.
Only a few minutes earlier, he had felt that same unnatural smoothness beneath his palm.
He tried to identify the shard through the Tower’s interface.
Nothing happened.
Then Leon called on the Cosmic System, expecting at least a name or some kind of category.
It gave him nothing.
That silence interested him more than a long description would have.
The Tower had named the Stalker and the crystal without hesitation. It had explained the trial, its dangers, and its rewards. Yet it refused to acknowledge the black fragment.
It had treated the black door the same way.
Leon turned the sliver in his fingers and looked at the broken marking.
The door has no symbol. This carries part of one.
One piece couldn’t reveal the full design, but the fractured edge proved something. The shard had once been part of a larger object.
Maybe other optional guardians held more fragments.
Maybe they could only be found in certain hidden areas.
Leon had no idea how many existed or what collecting them would do. What he did know was that the shard and the sealed door seemed to share the same material.
That was enough.
He stored the black fragment apart from the Spatial Tempering Crystal.
A low rumble moved through the chamber.
Leon stood and drew his sword, but no enemy appeared.
Behind the pedestal, the stone wall began to separate. Sections folded inward with precise mechanical movement, opening onto a wide intersection.
More than a dozen passages extended from the new area.

Some archways carried an engraved key. Others displayed an open treasure chest. The remaining routes had no markings at all. Dim light reached only a short distance into those corridors before darkness swallowed the rest.
The floor’s design had become clearer.
Key paths moved the required trial forward.
Treasure paths improve both the challenger and the Gatekeeper.
The unmarked routes offered no explanation.
Before Leon chose, a faint disturbance passed through the corridor behind him.
It came from the circular room where the trial had started.
The sealed black door pulsed once.
His spatial awareness still couldn’t enter it, but the ripple spreading from its surface was impossible to miss. At the same time, the black fragment in storage gave a small vibration.
Then both stopped.
Leon smiled.
The fragment belonged to the hidden route. He still didn’t know how many pieces were needed, but now he had a reason to search for them.
He stepped into the intersection and studied the choices ahead.
The floor only required three Tower Keys. Finding them and leaving would be the safest option, especially now that the Gatekeeper possessed Spatial Resistance.
But the labyrinth offered much more than three mandatory routes.

Epic treasures waited inside it. Adaptive guardians protected them. Unmarked passages led to unknown places, and hidden fragments connected to a door that neither the Tower nor the Cosmic System would explain.
Completing only the required objective would mean walking away from most of the floor’s value.

Leon still wasn’t going to throw himself into every chamber without thought. Permanent death remained permanent, no matter how good the reward looked. He would examine each route, keep track of what enhancements he gave the Gatekeeper, and withdraw from anything beyond what he could safely handle.
Greed and caution could exist together.
An idiot took everything simply because it was there.
Someone capable made sure the price wouldn’t kill him.
Leon compared the nearest entrances. Two were marked by bronze keys. Another carried the silver image of a treasure chest. Farther down, an unmarked corridor bent out of view.
His hand settled on his sword’s hilt.
Three keys were enough to clear the floor.
Anything else would strengthen the Gatekeeper.
Leon’s attention went to the silver route first.
Collect three keys and leave? In a place like this, that would be a waste.
He made his choice and continued deeper into the labyrinth.

Interesting did not mean he would claim everything blindly.
One reward had given him something directly useful.
From this point on, every optional route would have to justify both its own danger and the ability it granted the Gatekeeper.
He left the pedestal and returned to the Stalker’s body.
Before moving on, he wanted another look at the guardian’s core.
Its internal structure might prove useful once he eventually absorbed the crystal.
The metal beneath its head had split where Leon’s sword went through.
Broken channels spread around the destroyed core, most of them dark now that the construct’s energy had disappeared.
Something black rested among them.
Leon crouched beside the remains.
The object hadn’t been inside the core.
It had been hidden behind it.
His earlier spatial examination missed the thing because it carried no energy and blended into the empty space around the Stalker’s central mechanisms.
He eased it loose.
It was a narrow shard of black material, a little longer than his thumb.
One side was perfectly smooth.
The opposite edge had broken unevenly.
A faint design had been pressed into its surface, but the marking ended at the fracture before it could form anything he recognized.
No mana came from it.
There was no aura or spiritual presence either.
Even its weight felt hard to measure.
Leon rubbed a thumb over the flawless surface.
The sealed black door came to mind at once.
Only a few minutes earlier, he had felt that same unnatural smoothness beneath his palm.
He tried to identify the shard through the Tower’s interface.
Nothing happened.
Then Leon called on the Cosmic System, expecting at least a name or some kind of category.
It gave him nothing.
That silence interested him more than a long description would have.
The Tower had named the Stalker and the crystal without hesitation.
It had explained the trial, its dangers, and its rewards.
Yet it refused to acknowledge the black fragment.
It had treated the black door the same way.
Leon turned the sliver in his fingers and looked at the broken marking.
The door has no symbol.
This carries part of one.
One piece couldn’t reveal the full design, but the fractured edge proved something.
The shard had once been part of a larger object.
Maybe other optional guardians held more fragments.
Maybe they could only be found in certain hidden areas.
Leon had no idea how many existed or what collecting them would do.
What he did know was that the shard and the sealed door seemed to share the same material.
That was enough.
He stored the black fragment apart from the Spatial Tempering Crystal.
A low rumble moved through the chamber.
Leon stood and drew his sword, but no enemy appeared.
Behind the pedestal, the stone wall began to separate.
Sections folded inward with precise mechanical movement, opening onto a wide intersection.
More than a dozen passages extended from the new area.
Some archways carried an engraved key.
Others displayed an open treasure chest.
The remaining routes had no markings at all.
Dim light reached only a short distance into those corridors before darkness swallowed the rest.
The floor’s design had become clearer.
Key paths moved the required trial forward.
Treasure paths improve both the challenger and the Gatekeeper.
The unmarked routes offered no explanation.
Before Leon chose, a faint disturbance passed through the corridor behind him.
It came from the circular room where the trial had started.
The sealed black door pulsed once.
His spatial awareness still couldn’t enter it, but the ripple spreading from its surface was impossible to miss.
At the same time, the black fragment in storage gave a small vibration.
Then both stopped.
Leon smiled.
The fragment belonged to the hidden route.
He still didn’t know how many pieces were needed, but now he had a reason to search for them.
He stepped into the intersection and studied the choices ahead.
The floor only required three Tower Keys.
Finding them and leaving would be the safest option, especially now that the Gatekeeper possessed Spatial Resistance.
But the labyrinth offered much more than three mandatory routes.
Epic treasures waited inside it.
Adaptive guardians protected them.
Unmarked passages led to unknown places, and hidden fragments connected to a door that neither the Tower nor the Cosmic System would explain.
Completing only the required objective would mean walking away from most of the floor’s value.
Leon still wasn’t going to throw himself into every chamber without thought.
Permanent death remained permanent, no matter how good the reward looked.
He would examine each route, keep track of what enhancements he gave the Gatekeeper, and withdraw from anything beyond what he could safely handle.
Greed and caution could exist together.
An idiot took everything simply because it was there.
Someone capable made sure the price wouldn’t kill him.
Leon compared the nearest entrances.
Two were marked by bronze keys.
Another carried the silver image of a treasure chest.
Farther down, an unmarked corridor bent out of view.
His hand settled on his sword’s hilt.
Three keys were enough to clear the floor.
Anything else would strengthen the Gatekeeper.
Leon’s attention went to the silver route first.
Collect three keys and leave?
In a place like this, that would be a waste.
He made his choice and continued deeper into the labyrinth.

chapters.title: Chapter 565: What It Witnesses, It Claims
paragraphs: The silver-marked corridor was much shorter than the trapped one, and there was almost no sound inside it.
Leon still advanced with care.
An empty-looking hallway in the Tower meant nothing. He spread his perception ahead of him with every step, checking for hidden wires, pressure tiles, and any sign that space had been altered.
There was nothing.
The corridor ran straight and narrow. Only the walls drew his attention.

Their texture changed as he moved deeper. The dark stone slowly lost its rough grain and became smooth, then smoother still, until a faint shine spread across the surface. After another dozen steps, Leon noticed a distorted bronze-gold figure moving beside him.
His reflection.
By the time he reached the next room, both sides of the passage had turned into mirrors.

The chamber beyond had eight sides. Each wall consisted of one unbroken panel of dark glass. The floor carried the same black polish, reflecting everything so clearly that it looked as though another room hung upside down under Leon’s feet.
He remained at the entrance and examined the eight versions of himself surrounding the chamber.
They didn’t all move correctly.
Most followed him, but some reacted a fraction of a second late. Two reflections to his right moved before he did.
One of them lifted its head and looked across the room before Leon had decided to turn that way. When Leon followed its gaze, the reflection was already looking back at him.
He kept his face neutral and gave no sign that he had noticed.

A translucent barrier sealed off the far side of the chamber. Beyond it floated a silver-black crystal shaped like a fragment from a shattered mirror. Whenever light touched it, the beam bent and returned from the wrong direction.
Leon could judge its grade without crossing the room.
Epic.
The urge to take it came immediately.
Later. There is always a guardian.
He stepped into the chamber and kept watching the mirrors.
The delayed reflections slipped farther behind. The ones moving early continued to lead him. One showed Leon already standing in the middle of the room, arms loose at his sides.
A moment later, Leon reached that exact position.
Every reflection vanished.
All eight mirror walls became completely black.
Leon’s hand shifted toward his sword as the largest panel began to ripple like water after a stone had struck it.
A figure walked out.
Its body was humanoid and formed from polished dark silver. It matched Leon’s height closely, but there were no features on its face or hands.
Then its head began to change.

The brow appeared first. A nose followed, then a mouth and jaw. The creature was recreating Leon’s face, though it didn’t get the details quite right. One eye sat higher than the other, and the mouth was stretched slightly too far.
It looked enough like him to feel wrong.
Messages appeared in the air between them.
[Optional Trial: Covetous Reflection]
[Defeat the guardian to claim the treasure.]
[Warning: What it witnesses, it may claim.]
Leon read the final line a second time.
The Tower had warned him what kind of threat he faced, but it had left the rules vague. He would have to work them out during the fight.

The dormant reinforcement inside the Reflection sat around Ethereal Initiate level, a rank Leon could already handle before his recent growth. Whatever made this guardian meaningful would come from the ability the Tower had warned him about, not from its starting power.
The Reflection didn’t move.
"Fine. We’ll start small."
Leon lifted his empty hand and created a basic fire attack. He kept the technique intentionally weak, forming a compact burst of flame that barely required any concentration.
The fire crossed the room and struck the guardian in the chest.
Flames scattered over the silver surface without leaving so much as a mark.
The Reflection raised one hand.
A matching flame appeared in its palm.

Leon focused on the copy. Its shape and color were almost identical, though the energy inside it was lower. When the creature fired, the attack seemed to carry about two-thirds of the force Leon had used.
He compressed a short section of space and shifted three feet to the left. The flame passed through the place where he had been and exploded against the mirror behind him.
The Reflection followed him with its uneven eyes.
It raised its hand once more.
The space beside it folded.

Leon sensed the attempt immediately because of how rough it was. The creature forced the surrounding space into place instead of controlling it through understanding. Even so, it had reproduced the basic form of Leon’s displacement.
The Reflection disappeared and returned several feet away.
Another imitation of his flame had already begun forming in its hand.
Leon’s expression hardened.
What it witnesses, it may claim.
The guardian had seen each active technique once and copied both.

That did not mean it could recreate everything Leon possessed. Its fire was weaker than his, and its spatial movement lacked the precision Void Dominion gave him. It seemed able to reproduce the structure of an ability without inheriting the foundation that supported it.
But that conclusion rested on only two examples.
Leon wasn’t going to reveal his entire arsenal just to test the theory.

Leximancy, Elemental Surge, Raijin, the deeper applications of Void Dominion, and his strongest elemental combinations remained unused. Even if one of them could end the trial immediately, showing a copying guardian the structure of his best abilities before he understood its limits would be foolish.

A second element might give the Reflection another kind of attack. A stronger use of space could teach it a more dangerous movement technique. Every ability he exposed might become another weapon aimed back at him.
The Reflection displaced itself without warning.
It appeared on Leon’s right and released its copied flame at close range.
Leon drew his sword as he turned. The attack struck the flat of the blade, split around it, and washed across his conscious armor.
Heat rolled over the bronze-gold surface.
A silver bar pushed out from the Reflection’s forearm. It lengthened until it formed the rough shape of a sword.
The guardian attacked before the flames had cleared.
Leon met the crude blade with his own.
Metal struck metal with a sharp crash.
The Reflection pressed closer, its flawed copy of Leon’s face directly before him. Its eyes followed the placement of his feet, the turn of his shoulders, and every adjustment of his sword.
The creature wasn’t merely taking his abilities.
It was learning how he fought.

chapters.title: Chapter 566: It Could Not Copy His Judgment
paragraphs: Leon knocked the Reflection’s weapon away and followed with two simple attacks.
The first was meant to probe its defense.
The second made it shift its right foot.
Immediately afterward, the guardian placed its own feet in the same position Leon had used.
The copy was clumsy, but only for a moment. During their next clash, the Reflection corrected its balance, adjusted the height of its blade to match Leon’s, and began stepping in the same rhythm.
It could study ordinary movements as easily as techniques.
Leon broke the pattern before it became comfortable. He cut high, changed his grip, then sent the blade low.
The Reflection blocked both.
Its second defense barely arrived in time. Leon stepped in, ready to take advantage.
The guardian folded space.
Its crude displacement carried it to his left. Before Leon finished turning, copied fire struck his shoulder and spread over his conscious armor.
The silver sword came directly behind it.
Its edge dragged across the bronze-gold surface, leaving a bright line from shoulder to chest. The force drove Leon back two steps.
His armor flowed over the mark and erased it within seconds.
The Reflection watched closely.
It did not create armor of its own.
So far, it had reproduced techniques Leon consciously performed and movements it could observe. The living armor acted independently, which might place it beyond the guardian’s ability to copy.
Leon refused to treat that as certain.
A few exchanges were nowhere near enough to understand every limit of an unknown Tower guardian.
They continued trading blows.
Anything Leon repeated became a liability. On the third use of the same sidestep, the Reflection moved early and positioned its blade where he should have ended up.
His instincts warned him.

Leon halted halfway through the motion, turned his hips, and guided the silver edge past his ribs. His return strike landed in the center of the guardian’s chest, but the sword failed to break through. Adaptive reinforcement gathered against his force, turning what looked like ordinary silver into a defense calibrated to him.
The Reflection withdrew.

Its borrowed face had improved. The higher eye had lowered into place. Its mouth and jaw now matched Leon’s proportions, while its stance had grown close enough to his that the fight resembled a duel against an imperfect image.
The creature could copy where he put his feet.
It could match the angle of his sword.
What it did not possess was the experience that decided how one action should lead into the next.

Leon carried nine integrated years of experience from a warrior who had survived more fights than this construct could ever stand around and watch. That experience gave him more than the memory of how to swing a blade. It let him feel commitment, hesitation, and poor balance before his conscious mind had finished sorting out what he saw.
The Reflection learned a movement once it witnessed it.
It could not take the judgment behind that movement.
Leon chose to build the fight around that weakness.
He advanced with a direct thrust along the center line. The technique was deliberately plain, the sort of motion taught to someone on their first day with a sword.
The Reflection stopped it with its forearm.
Leon pulled back before the counterattack came and returned to guard.
The guardian had now seen the thrust.
Next, he had to teach it to believe that seeing was enough.
They fought through several ordinary exchanges. Leon reused pieces of his earlier rhythm and allowed the Reflection to become increasingly confident in its predictions.
The silver guardian began pressing him.

It mixed copied fire with short spatial folds, shifting between angles while using footwork taken from Leon. Neither copied technique equalled the original, but together they forced him to defend against attacks from multiple directions.
Another blow clipped his armored shoulder.
The armor endured.
Leon retreated and recreated the opening from before.
His feet settled into the same stance used for the center-line thrust. His sword lowered to the same angle. His body appeared open in exactly the same place.
The Reflection recognized it.
This time, it did not wait to defend.
It launched the copied thrust first, attempting to hit Leon before his expected attack could begin.
Its weight committed forward.
His instincts caught that commitment at once.
Leon discarded the thrust.
He dropped his point and stepped outside the line the guardian expected. The silver weapon passed beside his ribs, while the Reflection’s own momentum carried it into the gap Leon had offered.
Its core became exposed for the first time.
Leon moved inside the reach of its blade and drove his sword through the middle of its chest.
The Reflection tried to correct itself.
Its torso twisted as it attempted to copy Leon’s new angle, but too much of its weight had already gone into the stolen attack. By the time it witnessed the change, it was too late to use it.
Holy energy ran down Leon’s blade.
The core broke.
Silver light flashed weakly through the construct. Leon’s copied face smoothed away, and the weapon extending from its arm melted back into the limb.
The guardian collapsed onto the polished floor.
Leon kept his sword ready until the last trace of energy vanished.
[Optional Guardian Defeated: Covetous Reflection]
[Optional Treasure Available]
[Mirrorheart Tempering Shard — Epic]
[Effect: Strengthens resistance against copied, stolen, reflected, or imitated versions of the bearer’s abilities when absorbed.]
The barrier sealing the far end of the room disappeared.
Leon walked toward the floating shard.
Its mirrored surface showed him a distorted face, one eye positioned higher than the other. The flawed image vanished as soon as he closed his hand around the crystal.
He placed it in storage beside the Spatial Tempering Crystal.
Neither Epic treasure would be absorbed until he reached somewhere secure. Integrating one while still inside an active Tower trial would leave him exposed.
The Tower registered the choice.
[Optional Treasures Claimed: 2]
[Gatekeeper Enhancement Applied]
[The Gatekeeper has acquired Technique Mimicry.]
Leon stared at the last message.
The Gatekeeper could now resist spatial abilities and might be able to reproduce techniques used against it.
Whether its Technique Mimicry carried the same limitations as the Reflection’s remained unknown.
The Tower gave him nothing else.
Once again, Leon had made the final encounter more dangerous.
Even so, the Mirrorheart Tempering Shard had been worth claiming.
He simply had to remember that every reward he took reshaped the enemy waiting at the end.

chapters.title: Chapter 567: The Door in the Mirror
paragraphs: Leon looked back at what remained of the Covetous Reflection.

His spatial perception had noticed a small inconsistency behind the shattered core. There was no energy there, no spiritual presence, only a tiny gap in the surrounding metal where something seemed to be missing from reality.
He crouched beside the fallen construct and pried the hidden object free with two fingers.
Another black fragment lay in his palm.
It matched the first piece. The surface was smooth and impossibly deep, swallowing light without giving back even the faintest reflection. An unfinished pattern ran across one side.
The Tower displayed nothing.
The Cosmic System stayed silent too.
Leon took out the first fragment and held the two pieces close together.
The broken edges pulled toward one another.
He loosened his fingers and let them shift. They aligned on their own, and the partial lines across both fragments joined into a larger section of the same unknown symbol.
The pieces did not fuse.
Leon drew them apart without effort, then brought them close again. Each time, they returned to exactly the same position.
Even together, they revealed only part of the design. Several lines reached the fractured edges and stopped, making it obvious that additional pieces were missing.
He had no way to tell whether the fragments formed half the symbol or only a small fraction of it.
Still, finding a second one proved something.
Other optional guardians might be carrying more.
Leon stored both pieces together.
Something shifted in the mirror behind him.
He turned.
For less than a heartbeat, the panel no longer showed his reflection. A circular chamber of stone appeared inside it instead.
The black door stood there, recognizable at once by its flawless surface and the complete absence of reflected light.
This time, the door was open.
There was nothing beyond it except darkness.
Leon’s hand went toward his sword, but the image vanished before he could move. His reflection returned, alone in the polished chamber.
He watched the mirror.
Nothing else changed.
The black door had reacted to the fragments. Whether that brief vision had been a warning, an invitation, or simply an acknowledgment was impossible to know.
Whatever waited beyond it was aware that he was getting closer.
Leon left the chamber with two Epic treasures and two pieces of a mystery the Tower refused to recognize.
The silver corridor brought him back to the central intersection.

Bronze paths, silver paths, and unmarked routes surrounded him. He had already claimed two optional rewards without finding even one Tower Key. The Gatekeeper had gained Spatial Resistance and Technique Mimicry because of those choices.
Before making it stronger again, Leon wanted to see what the required paths demanded.
He chose a nearby bronze arch engraved with the image of a key.
Beyond it, a broad passage sloped downward. Long, shallow steps vanished into the dark.
Leon stepped through.
A seam split open in the floor behind him.
A bronze chain burst from the stone and wrapped around his left wrist. Before he could pull back, the final links fused into a solid band.
The rest of the chain dropped into the floor.
Tower messages appeared.
[Mandatory Key Trial: Burden of Possession]
[Reach the Key Chamber while bearing the weight of what you have claimed.]
[The burden increases with every optional treasure acquired.]
[The chain cannot be removed until the trial is completed or abandoned.]
[Burden calibrated to challenger.]
[Recovery from burden-inflicted strain is suspended while the chain remains sealed.]
Leon tried to lift his bound arm.
It barely rose.
Leon increased his physical reinforcement.
The chain grew heavier with him.

That explained the calibration. The Tower was not asking him to drag a fixed amount of bronze that his current body could throw through a wall. The burden scales against his usable strength, always claiming a punishing share of it. His mythical armor could spread the load. It could not make the trial forget how strong he was.

More concerning was the suppression spreading from the bronze band around his wrist. His mana circulation slowed. Energy that normally flowed through him freely now pushed through his channels like thick liquid. Life and holy energy still answered elsewhere, but anything he directed into the bound arm dispersed beneath the band before it could repair the accumulating strain.
The space around him felt resistant as well.
Leon attempted a minor fold, intending only to bring a few links closer.
The chain reacted at once.
Its weight doubled.
Suppression clamped down around his energy channels, and pain stabbed through his wrist. Leon released the technique and allowed space to settle back into place.
The burden slowly returned to its previous level.
Spatial displacement would probably trigger the same response. Elemental Surge or a larger reinforcement would only give the chain more strength to measure and more weight to return.
So much for avoiding the weight.
The chain represented the two optional treasures he had taken. Had he claimed more before entering a key route, the calibrated share would have been worse.
The Gatekeeper was the final cost of greed.
This trial collected payment before he ever reached it.
Leon started down the corridor.
As he moved, fresh links rose from the floor behind him while those farther back sank into the stone. The chain kept the same length and pull no matter how far he traveled.
He stopped and examined it.
The chain was not fixed to the entrance. Its real anchor moved beneath the floor with him, ensuring that he could neither leave it behind nor reach its source.
Abandoning the trial would presumably remove it.
Leon had not entered with any intention of turning back.
He rolled his shoulder, adjusted his grip on his sword, and looked down the descending passage.
He had chosen to take the treasures.
Now the Tower intended to make him carry them.
Leon continued downward.
At first, the route was only steep.
He leaned into the descent and let his strengthened legs absorb the strain. Bronze links continued rising behind him and vanishing once he passed.
The weight never changed.

Each step pulled at his left shoulder, while the band around his wrist kept slowing his energy. His conscious armor thickened around the joint, spreading part of the pressure across his chest and back.
That support kept the arm usable.
The chain adjusted and preserved the burden.
The steps moved beneath him.
His instincts caught the shift before the entire staircase tilted sharply to the left. Leon dropped his center of gravity as the chain pulled him toward the edge.
A deep pit opened beside the stairs.
He planted his feet and let the armor around his knees and hips harden into a stronger frame. His boots scraped across the stone, but he held his position until the staircase returned to level.
Pain ran from his wrist into his shoulder.
The Tower gave him almost no time to recover.

Ahead, the corridor narrowed. Rotating bronze pillars filled the path, each fitted with blunt projections that swept through the available space at different heights. Brief gaps opened between them, then vanished.
Without the chain, Leon could have crossed the obstacle in seconds.
He watched the pattern twice before moving.
Leon slipped past the first pillar and dragged the chain after him. Several trailing links caught around one of the projections.
The next pillar turned toward his ribs while the snagged chain jerked his left arm backward.
Instead of fighting the pull, Leon rotated with it.
The motion carried him close enough to slash at the base of the projection. His sword severed the joint, and the bronze bar crashed to the floor.
He pulled the chain free and moved before the next pillar reached him.
A second snag almost dragged him beneath a rotating column. Leon let the chain pull his arm behind him, ducked under the sweeping bar, and used the momentum to carry himself into the next safe gap.
He passed through the final opening just as two pillars closed behind him.
Sweat gathered beneath his armor.
Feeling had begun to fade from his left hand.
The route continued along a thin ledge overlooking another pit with no visible bottom. There was barely enough space for both boots, and the chain hung from the side nearest the drop.
Its weight pulled straight down.
Leon pressed his right shoulder against the wall and advanced one careful step at a time. His armor reinforced his ankles, knees, and hips while his instincts managed the constant shifts in balance.
A section of ledge broke beneath his leading foot.
He withdrew before putting his full weight on it.
The chain used the moment to drag him toward the pit.
Leon drove his sword into a crack in the wall and caught himself with his right arm.
Fragments of stone fell into the darkness.
No sound came back.
He waited until his balance returned, pulled the sword free, and moved on.
The chain fought him with every step. His left shoulder scraped against the wall as he leaned away from the drop, and the muscles around the joint began to tremble despite the armor supporting them.
Near the middle, the ledge became even narrower.
Leon turned sideways and moved one foot at a time.
A sudden pulse traveled through the chain, sharply increasing its downward pull.
His boot slipped.

His sharp instincts drove his hips toward the wall before his conscious thoughts caught up. Leon dropped to one knee, gripped the ledge with his right hand, and endured the added weight until the pulse faded.
Then he stood and kept moving.
By the time he reached the far side, his chained arm was shaking.
Leon allowed himself three breaths.
No more.
Two bronze sentinels unfolded from alcoves ahead.
They stood shorter than Leon, but each was nearly twice his width. Heavy armor covered their bodies. Neither carried a weapon.
Their oversized fists were enough.
The first sentinel charged.

chapters.title: Chapter 568: The First Tower Key
paragraphs: Leon kept his chained arm tucked close to his body and relied on one-handed swordwork.
The first sentinel opened with a heavy punch. He slipped past it and cut across the construct’s neck, but the blade only gouged a shallow line into the bronze.
The material was not truly resisting him by its ordinary grade. Adaptive Tower reinforcement thickened at the point of impact, scaling the sentinel’s defense against the strength behind his cut.
The second sentinel came in from his left.
Its approach forced Leon closer to the pit.
Rather than retreat, he moved inside the first construct’s reach.
A bronze fist crashed into his conscious armor. The impact drove a thick jolt through his ribs, but it also left the first sentinel standing directly between Leon and the other one.
The second construct threw its punch.
Leon ducked.
The blow struck its companion in the head and knocked it sideways.
Before the damaged sentinel could recover, Leon drove his sword into the groove at its neck joint.
The first construct dropped.
The remaining sentinel reached for the bronze band around Leon’s wrist.
His instincts guided him under its arms. Leon cut through the rear of one knee, brought the construct down, then thrust his sword into the opening beneath its helmet.
The second sentinel went still.
Leon pulled his blade free and kept moving down the passage.

The chain became heavier as he approached the Key Chamber. The trial was increasing its pressure for the final guardian. Suppression continued grinding through his energy channels, and his left hand felt like a cold, useless weight hanging from his wrist.
At last, the corridor opened into a chamber.
The room was wide with a low ceiling. A bronze key floated over a pedestal on the far side.
A guardian blocked the way.
It stood a full head and shoulders taller than Leon and wore heavy bronze armor from helmet to boots. In one hand, it carried a shield nearly as broad as a door.
Its other hand gripped a long staff tipped with a curved hook.
Leon looked from the hook to the chain on his wrist.
A message appeared.
[Mandatory Guardian: Bronze Tollkeeper]

The construct’s own movement and gathered force reached the upper range of Ethereal Initiate. That alone would not have troubled Leon. The danger came from its connection to the calibrated burden wrapped around his wrist.
The construct raised its shield and started forward.
Its hooked staff swept for Leon’s chain.
Leon moved to avoid it.
Before finishing the swing, the Tollkeeper changed the angle. The hook missed his leg, slid beneath the chain, and twisted.
The bronze links drew tight.
Then the guardian pulled.
The force used the calibrated burden against Leon’s restrained arm and dragged him across the floor. He brought his sword up, but the shield reached him first.
Its edge smashed into his armored forearm.
His conscious armor absorbed enough force to keep the bone intact. The impact still threw him aside.
Leon landed hard and rolled before the hooked staff could come down on his skull.
The chain was still trapped.
Another yank hauled him toward the shield.
Leon planted his boots and pulled back.
For several seconds, the chain stretched taut between them. Stone scraped beneath his feet while pain burned through his shoulder.
The Tollkeeper was connected to the trial mechanism. Every pull on its hook let the burden match Leon’s resistance, giving the construct leverage no fixed-rank body should have possessed.
Trying to win through strength would only waste what little Leon had left.
He stopped resisting.
Leon moved with the pull.
The sudden loss of tension unsettled the guardian’s balance. Leon rushed toward it, adding his own speed and strength to the force dragging him across the chamber.
He crossed the shield’s outer edge before the Tollkeeper adjusted.
His conscious armor reinforced his sword arm.
Leon slipped around the guardian’s back and drove his blade into the seam beneath its helmet.
The metal split apart.
His sword sank several inches before striking a tougher layer underneath.
The Tollkeeper turned with unexpected speed.
Its shield swung backward and slammed into Leon’s side, ripping the sword from the damaged seam. The blow sent him skidding across the chamber.
The guardian stayed upright.
A thin line of bronze light leaked from the wound in its neck, but Leon had failed to reach the core.
He rose with care.
The Tollkeeper had learned from that exchange.
It shortened its grip on the hooked staff and angled its shield toward the injured side of its neck. If it caught Leon’s chain again, it would not leave him enough space to get behind it.
The construct advanced.
This time, the hook caught the chain closer to Leon’s wrist.
The pull was short and violent.
Leon stepped into it, but the Tollkeeper expected that response. Its shield turned to meet him.
He dropped beneath the lower edge.
The guardian immediately drove the shield downward, trying to crush him against the floor. Leon rolled clear, but the hooked staff reversed direction and jerked his chained arm behind him.
His shoulder reached its limit.
The conscious armor thickened around the joint before anything tore.
Pain still burst down Leon’s side.
He slashed at the staff.
His sword carved a deep notch into the bronze shaft without cutting through it.
The Tollkeeper pulled him closer.
As the chain tightened, Leon noticed how it crossed in front of the guardian’s shield arm.
An idea came together.
He quit fighting the pull and charged forward again.
This time, he made no attempt to slip around the shield.
Leon planted one foot against its lower edge and vaulted upward.
The Tollkeeper lifted the shield, trying to throw him away.
Leon twisted over the top while carrying his chained wrist across it. The bronze links slid around the shield’s rim and dropped behind the guardian’s elbow.
He landed with the chain looped around the Tollkeeper’s shield arm.
The guardian pulled with its hooked staff.
The chain tightened around its own limb.
Its shield arm snapped outward, dragged away from the wounded side of its neck.
The Tollkeeper let go of the staff with one hand and reached to untangle itself.
Leon gave it no chance.
He stepped onto the stretched chain and used it as temporary footing. His armor reinforced both legs and his right shoulder as he launched himself upward.
Then he drove his sword down into the existing wound.
The blade punched through the damaged inner layer.
Holy energy surged along the steel and poured into the guardian.
The Tollkeeper swung the hooked staff at him.
Leon turned his armored side into the strike and accepted the hit rather than give up the attack.
The hook cracked against the bronze-gold surface.
Leon shoved the sword deeper.
The core shattered.
Light burst through the seams in the Tollkeeper’s armor, then faded.
Its shield slipped from its hand and struck the floor. The hooked staff fell beside it.
For one final moment, the guardian remained standing.
Then the entire construct collapsed.
The bronze band around Leon’s wrist opened.
Every chain link dropped onto the stone and became ordinary metal.
The weight disappeared.
So did the suppression.
Energy rushed through Leon’s restricted channels.
Pins and cold pain erupted through his left arm. He flexed his fingers while Life and holy energy poured through pathways the band had kept closed.

Torn fibers drew together. Swelling vanished. The deep strain from wrist to shoulder receded over the next several breaths, and full strength returned with it. His natural regeneration handled the rest while his mana reserve resumed its steady recovery.
Even without drawing more energy from the surroundings, his passive recovery replaced roughly three percent of what he had spent each minute.
Completing the trial had removed the restraint.
Leon’s body erased what the restraint had done to him.
Messages appeared above the fallen guardian.
[Tower Key Acquired]
[Tower Keys Collected: 1/3]
[Mandatory Key Trial Completed]
The bronze key rose from the Tollkeeper’s remains.
Leon caught it in his restored left hand.
It was plain and solid. Compared to either Epic treasure, it carried almost no overwhelming presence.
Obtaining it had still demanded more physical effort than claiming both optional rewards.
The keys were the real purpose of this floor.
Everything else only made reaching them more difficult.
Leon stored the first Tower Key beside the two unabsorbed crystals and the black fragments.
A section of wall opened at the back of the chamber.
The new passage did not return him to the earlier intersection. The labyrinth had shifted again, presenting three different routes.
A bronze key marked the first arch.
An open silver chest marked the second.
The last route had no symbol at all. Beyond its archway stretched a corridor so dark that even Leon’s enhanced vision could not pierce it.
Something moved inside his storage.
Both black fragments pulled in the same direction.
Their attraction was far stronger than before. They strained toward the unmarked passage like compass needles settling on north.
Something tied to the sealed black door waited down that route.
Leon considered all three choices.
The bronze passage would move him closer to clearing the floor.
The silver route promised another treasure and another enhancement for the Gatekeeper.
The black corridor offered no listed reward and served no official objective.
It was also the only path the Tower refused to recognize.
Leon now carried one Tower Key, two unabsorbed Epic treasures, and two unidentified fragments. The Gatekeeper waiting at the end had already gained Spatial Resistance and Technique Mimicry.
Taking another optional route would strengthen it again.
The bronze path was safer.
It was also the practical choice.
The fragments pulled toward the darkness once more.
Leon’s eyes settled on the unmarked corridor.
This time, he did not look away.
